standard_prerequisites: Same chapter: lemma-take-pth-root (if alpha is not a p-th power in L then T^p - alpha is irreducible over L); separability of L/K gives the minimal polynomial of alpha pairwise distinct roots
core_obligations: Reduction: (2) implies (1) by taking P to be the minimal polynomial of alpha over K
Build Q from P by replacing each coefficient a_i = b_i^p with b_i; the roots of Q are the p-th roots of the roots of P, so Q also has pairwise distinct roots

Contradiction: if alpha is not a p-th power, T^p - alpha is irreducible over L (lemma-take-pth-root) and shares the root alpha of Q in an algebraic closure, so T^p - alpha divides Q in L[T], forcing Q to have a repeated root
proof_roadmap: Pass from P to its coefficient-wise p-th root polynomial Q
Run the irreducibility of T^p - alpha against divisibility to contradict distinctness
